stories.headline: Trump administration turns to SCOTUS in California ballot case
stories.summary: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to mandate that California separate ballots of more than 20,000 voters the government suspects are "likely" non-citizens. The big picture: A federal appeals court rejected the administration's bid to set aside mail ballots last week, erecting another roadblock in the DOJ's pre-election quest to demand the state root out claims of voter fraud in the final days of the midterm elections. Driving the news: "Once California commingles the challenged ballots with lawful ones, there is no way to get the challenged ballots back," the DOJ wrote in an… (Axios)

stories.headline: Young co-pilot, 20, named as one of nine victims of deadly Florida plane crash
stories.summary: Nathalia Filgueiras was onboard private plane bound for Bahamas that crashed in Palm Beach county Family members on Monday identified a young Florida pilot as one of nine victims of a plane crash in Palm Beach county that occurred during a heavy thunderstorm. Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, was co-pilot of the private Learjet 60 that was en route from Austin-Bergstrom international airport in Texas to North Eleuthera airport in the Bahamas on Sunday when it suddenly plummeted out of the sky, her mother told the New York Times . stories.headline: Hackers send fake nuclear threat alert to Ukraine emergency app
stories.summary: Residents in Kyiv also warned of chemical attack and street-to-street fighting in false message sent by unknown party Europe live – latest updates Unknown hackers have targeted Ukraine’s nationwide emergency alert mobile app, sending residents in Kyiv a warning that they were at risk of an imminent nuclear strike. The app reported a high possibility of nuclear radiation late on Sunday. It also wrongly warned of a chemical threat to the Ukrainian capital and street-to-street fighting. The messages were written in English with spelling mistakes, as well as in Ukrainian. Continue reading... (The Guardian (World))

stories.headline: Lindsay Clancy back in court seeking to dismiss murder charges after mistrial
stories.summary: Lawyers for Massachusetts mother who killed children argue new trial would violate double jeopardy rules Lindsay Clancy returned to court on Monday in an attempt to dismiss the charges that she murdered her three young children. The hearing Monday was the second time the Massachusetts mother has been in court since her trial ended with a deadlocked jury in September after jurors were unable to agree on a verdict.
